posts.caption:
IISER Bhopal celebrated National Youth Day and Swami Vivekananda Jayanti with a three-day event that united students through activities focused on physical and mental well-being, leadership, and community engagement.

From rejuvenating Yoga and Surya Namaskar sessions that promoted mindfulness and physical fitness, the campus truly embodied the spirit of youth.

The celebrations also witnessed stimulating intellectual discourse through the Youth Solution Assembly, where students voiced innovative ideas on contemporary socio-economic challenges. This was followed by a speech competition themed on leadership, civic responsibility, and nation-building.

The events were organized in association with the Yuva Bharat Club and the Counseling Cell, IISER Bhopal.

Through these initiatives, IISER Bhopal reaffirmed its commitment to nurturing confident, socially responsible, and empowered youth, in resonance with the ideals of Swami Vivekananda.

राष्ट्रीय युवा दिवस 2026
National Youth Day Celebration 2026
उठो, जागो और लक्ष्य की प्राप्ति तक बढ़ते चलो !
On the occasion of National Youth Day, the Yuva Bharat Club, in collaboration with the Counselling Cell, cordially invites all members of the IISER Bhopal community to participate in a Yoga and Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation) session.
Surya Namaskar is a sequence of twelve powerful yoga postures that offers a comprehensive full-body workout while promoting physical, mental, and emotional well-being. It is a meaningful practice to express gratitude to the Sun, the source of energy that sustains life on Earth. Owing to its simplicity and adaptability, the practice is suitable for participants of all age groups and fitness levels.
Let us come together to perform Surya Namaskar in unison and celebrate the spirit of youth, health, and harmony on National Youth Day 2026.
Details of the Event: 
Date: Saturday, 10 January 2026
Time: 7:00 AM 
Venue: LHC Atrium

posts.caption:
The CYC hosted an Interdisciplinary Youth Dialogue on Climate Action on 1 November 2025 at Indian Institute of Science, Education & Research, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, India, bringing together students and young leaders from science, policy, social sciences, technology, and community-based fields. 

The idea was simple yet powerful climate solutions demand cross-disciplinary thinking. When diverse minds meet, the conversation shifts from isolated ideas to shared pathways and collective responsibility.

Organised by the Commonwealth Youth Council in partnership with Jungle Vase, and in collaboration with the Student Development Council, Yuva Bharat Club, and the Environment & Social Initiative Council of IISER, the dialogue featured thematic roundtables and open exchanges that encouraged critical reflection, creativity, and grounded, youth-driven climate perspectives.

The discussions were thoughtful, energetic, and rooted in reality, highlighting that meaningful climate action isn’t about a single discipline, but about students, researchers, and young changemakers learning from one another and shaping solutions together.

#GetYouthInvolved

posts.caption:
Today, the Climate Convergence report was formally presented to the Director, IISER Bhopal by
Ankit Srivastava (Coordinator, Yuva Bharat Club), Vanshika Nandwana (Secretary, ESIC), Shlok Saraf (Secretary, SDC), Apoorva Sharad (Doctoral student & COP29 delegate) and Dr. Apurba Lal Koner.

The report captures key insights, recommendations and youth-led action plans that emerged from Climate Convergence at IISER Bhopal—an interdisciplinary dialogue on climate science, policy, innovation and just, sustainable lifestyles. 

Grateful to the Institute leadership for their constant encouragement and for empowering students to take the lead in climate action, community outreach and evidence-based policymaking. This is one more step towards making IISER Bhopal a hub for climate-conscious research, education and societal impact.

Youth Dialogue towards green future!
Climate Convergence 2025 | Interdisciplinary Youth Dialogue on Climate Action 

A dynamic platform where students, researchers & experts came together to co-create pathways toward sustainability and climate resilience — in collaboration with Commonwealth Youth Council (CYC) and Jungle Vase.

Inspiring insights from Dr. Lokendra Thakkar (EPCO, Govt. of MP), Mr. Imteyaz Ali (Sarthak Sanstha, Bhopal), and Dr. Sanjit Konar (DoFA, IISERB) reminded us that true change begins when awareness turns into collective action. 

Grateful to IISER Bhopal, SDC, ESIC, and Yuva Bharat Club for making this youth-led dialogue a success. Together, we move toward a sustainable future where empathy meets innovation.
